svg.title: A 22-year-old man received his first doses of haloperidol yesterday for a first episode of psychosis. This morning his neck is pulled hard to the left and his eyes are rolled upward and will not come down. He is frightened, drooling, and his speech is thick. There is no stridor. Temperature 37.0 °C, HR 104, BP 138/82, RR 20. Limb tone is normal.
svg.desc: Acute dystonia starts within about 96 hours of beginning or increasing a dopamine blocker, and torticollis with oculogyric crisis is the classic pair; parenteral diphenhydramine or benztropine usually resolves it in 10 to 30 minutes. The airway is watched because the same reaction can involve the larynx, and stridor is the warning sign of obstruction. Tardive dyskinesia is the tempting answer because it is also a movement disorder, but it appears after months to years and is not relieved by anticholinergics.
